Hi Samir / Lena —

Thanks again for carving out time yesterday — great context on the multi-domain search assistant you’re building and the latency targets (<=180ms 95th) for query-side completions. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can scope the eval and get you meaningful model recommendations: 

What we’ll do next (high level)
- Collect a ~2k sample of representative queries (mix of short queries, long contextual ones, and the 50 edge cases you flagged)
- Run a multi-model bench (Redwood-Base-7B-quant, Redwood-13B-pt, and a latency-optimized 4-bit variant) against your query mix with your 20k doc index snapshot
- Surface quality regressions on your critical prompt set (3 evaluation metrics: exact-match intents, helpfulness score, hallucination rate)
- Deliver a short report and prioritized remediation recommendations (prompt changes, caching, quantization suggestion)

What we need from DocuZen
1) Representative query batch (CSV or newline-delimited). For privacy we prefer samples with redacted PII — see guidance below.
2) Top 50 edge cases (examples that fail today or are high-risk) with short notes on expected behavior.
3) One anchor prompt template you use in production for relevance + answer synthesis.

Attached: sample_manifest.csv (format we use for ingestion) and example_queries.txt with the CSV headers.

Suggested models for the first pass
- redwood-base-7b-quant (good cost/latency tradeoff for interactive Q&A)
- redwood-13b-pt (higher quality, useful if you need better synthesis)
- redwood-latency-4bit (experimental, for tight SLOs but may show slight quality variance)

Redaction & upload options (short)
- If you can share redacted samples, remove any direct PII (names, SSNs, emails, account IDs) and replace with consistent tokens (e.g., [PERSON_1], [ACCOUNT_42]).
- If redaction is complex, we can receive data in a secured S3 bucket (we’ll provide a presigned URL) and handle redaction on our side under a temporary NDAed intake process — let us know which you prefer.

Timeline
- If we get the sample by EOD Thu (May 23), we’ll run the bench and get a first-results deck by Tue (May 28).

Next steps
- Samir: share either redacted samples or confirm secure upload option.
- Ben / Marissa / me: we’ll stand up the job and share the presigned link if needed.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short HubSpot note and the presigned link if you prefer secure upload.

Best,

Mina Haddad

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — sample queries, redaction, and model-recs

Samir —

Short answers: yes and yes, with caveats. A few specifics that should help you pick an approach: 

Redaction guidance (recommended)
- Keep tokens consistent across a single session: if "Acme Corp" appears multiple times in a thread, replace all instances with [ORG_1] rather than free text. That preserves co-reference signals.
- Preserve structural elements: dates, invoice IDs can be tokenized (e.g., [DATE], [INVOICE_ID]) but try to keep numeric patterns (length, dashes) intact to avoid model confusion.
- Avoid over-scrubbing context words that signal intent (e.g., "refund", "contract", "invoice"). Replace only the identifying substrings.

Why: For intent/slot metrics we care more about the surrounding language than the literal token of the entity. Using consistent tokens preserves slot positions and co-reference, which keeps benchmarking meaningful.

Secure intake flow
- If you choose secure upload we will share a presigned S3 path (48h valid) and an intake form. We’ll log all access and delete samples after the bench run. Legal can add a one-paragraph amendment; I’ll loop in our legal contact if you want that route.

Format & manifest
- CSV with columns: sample_id, raw_query, redaction_notes, expected_behavior (one of {answerable, escalate, privacy_hold}), biz_unit.
- Example in sample_manifest.csv.

Model/eval specifics we’ll run
- Microbench: 2k queries across 3 models listed earlier; 1000 short queries (<8 tokens), 800 mid-length, 200 long/contextual (30–250 tokens).
- We’ll track 95th latency, per-model token cost, and a quality delta vs baseline (you can pick current-prod as baseline).

Next: If you confirm secure upload I’ll send the presigned link within the hour. Otherwise, please upload redacted CSV by Thu EOD.

I’ll also include a short prompt bank we use for synthesis evaluation so you can map expectations.

Thanks,
Mina
